project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 273 (System includes the incumbent policy in the candidate set, which returns a selected policy never worse on the fixed history)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 273 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the clause that makes §C5's selection *safe*, and the clause three siblings already cite by number without implementing — docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §C5 states it as the qualifier on the whole dreaming loop — *"The paper's selection guarantee carries over unchanged: because the candidate set includes ``π^0 = π_t``, the selected policy is no worse than the current one *on the fixed replay history*. Note the qualifier. It is a guarantee about replay score, not about future P&L."* — and §12.1 leans on it as the reason a refused winner is not a lost cycle: *"The paper's guarantee ``V^{m★} ≥ V^0`` holds on the *fixed history*"*. Two spellings in one new module, dreaming/incumbent.py, beside feature 270's single "dreaming" component. (1) The value — :func:`incumbent_candidate(source, *, version=None, parent_version=None)`: the incumbent policy's own source in, and ``π^0`` out as a candidate-shaped entry, *through the member's one spelling of a candidate's identity* (feature 271's :func:`~dreaming.reviser._code_hash_of`, the sha256 the reviser hashes with, imported rather than respelled for the reason that function's own docstring gives — *"the one spelling of a candidate's identity … so the two cannot disagree on what makes two revisions the same candidate"*). It answers a frozen, hand-written-``__slots__`` :class:`IncumbentCandidate` carrying the three facts a candidate is read for — ``module_id``, ``code_hash``, ``parent_version`` — and its ``source``, and **deliberately no ``revision_index``**: the incumbent is not one of the ``M`` revisions feature 271 produced, and feature 272's own candidate reader was written to admit exactly this (*"a genuine positive integer **or absent**"*, and its docstring names the case — *"273's incumbent — put back into the candidate set by a **sibling** feature — may well arrive as a different class carrying the same facts"*). An incumbent whose caller names no ``version`` is given the version the loop itself would have written for it: ``cand-`` prefixed digest of its code hash, the same default :func:`dreaming.reviser.candidate_module` derives, so a previous cycle's ``policy_revision.policy_version`` is reconstructible from the policy source alone. (2) The act of *including* — :func:`include_incumbent(candidates, source, *, version=None, parent_version=None)` — the candidate set feature 271 produced and the incumbent in, and the **widened** set out, with ``π^0`` **first**: the incumbent is the set's opening member because it is the policy in force, and appending it would make the loop's own report read as though a revision had been added rather than the incumbent restored. Both are **pure**: no store, no clock, no environment, no ``@register`` component — the shape :func:`dreaming.ladder.rejects_thin_pool`, feature 276's ceiling, feature 278's split, feature 279's rotation and feature 274's argmax all take, and a caller that only wants *the widened set* asks this and pays for nothing. What the second clause of the sentence — *"which returns a selected policy never worse on the fixed history"* — means here is stated and pinned rather than assumed: with ``π^0`` in the set, feature 274's argmax is taken over a tournament one of whose entrants is the current policy, so **every path of the loop either selects a candidate whose §7 objective is at least the incumbent's, or refuses** (a tie at the top is feature 274's refusal, and a missing objective is feature 274's refusal) — ``V^{m★} ≥ V^0`` by construction, exactly as §12.1's own words claim, and never by a check this module performs. Refusals are **rather than silently defaulting**, each naming what it is about: a source that is not non-empty text, a ``version`` or ``parent_version`` that is not ``None`` or non-empty text, candidates that are not a sequence of candidate modules (a bare string refused where many candidates belong, because Python would iterate its characters), a candidate whose ``module_id`` or ``code_hash`` is not non-empty text, and — the load-bearing one — an incumbent **already in the set**, by its ``module_id`` or by its ``code_hash``, so a loop that ran feature 273 twice, or a reviser that returned the incumbent's source verbatim, is refused rather than handing feature 274 an argmax over two entrants that are one policy. An **empty** candidate set is **admitted**, not refused: the whole of this feature is *adding one*, and a set that holds only ``π^0`` is §C5's guarantee at its most literal — the selected policy *is* the incumbent — the admission feature 276's ceiling already states for a zero revision count (*"do not run any revision is a caller's own business"*). One new error sibling under DreamingError, :class:`IncumbentRequestError`, and no code word: feature 273's verb is *includes* and its sentence mandates none, so every message opens with its subject, the stance :class:`~dreaming.errors.CapRequestError`, :class:`~dreaming.errors.RevisionCeilingError` and :class:`~dreaming.errors.HoldoutRequestError` state. The module mints no store face and no verdict of its own, because the sentence has no store act and its second clause is a theorem about feature 274's argmax rather than a judgment this module makes. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; no new table; the member's single "dreaming" component is untouched and the seat is not edited — feature 275's floor names that precedent and features 271, 274 and 279 followed it.
project_specification.existing_context:
The dreaming member (packages/dreaming) already implements the §C5 loop's acts as free functions beside feature 270's single "dreaming" component, and the chain this feature completes is already spelled by its neighbours. Feature 271 (dreaming.reviser) produces M candidate modules through revise_policy, each a frozen CandidateModule carrying source, code_hash, module_id, parent_version and revision_index (1..M — the class refuses a non-positive index, which is why the incumbent enters as a value of its own rather than as a CandidateModule); its _code_hash_of is the member's one spelling of a candidate's identity and its candidate_module defaults module_id to f"cand-{code_hash[:32]}". Its docstring states this feature's contract — *"with the incumbent recorded as each candidate's ``parent_version`` so feature 273 can add ``π^0 = π_t`` back into the candidate set"* — and its _validated_parent says the same of the parent field (*"it is the incumbent feature 273 adds back to the candidate set"*). Feature 272 (dreaming.sweep) evaluates each candidate against every stored world and persists one replay_score row per pair through the replay member's persist_replay_score; its _candidate_of reads module_id, code_hash and an **optional** revision_index — *"a genuine positive integer or absent"* — and its docstring names this feature as the reason: *"273's incumbent — put back into the candidate set by a sibling feature — may well arrive as a different class carrying the same facts."* Its own docstring disclaims this feature's clause three times over: *"It is not the production, the incumbent's return, the argmax or the bar. … putting ``π^0 = π_t`` back into the candidate set so the selection can never fall below the current policy is feature 273's."* Feature 274 (dreaming.select) takes the argmax over whatever candidate set it is handed and its docstring draws the boundary verbatim — *"It is not feature 273 either: 273 puts the incumbent back into the candidate set so the argmax never falls below the current policy, and this module takes the argmax over whatever candidate set it is handed — if the loop has run 273 first, the incumbent is one candidate among the set"* — while its tie refusal names this feature's guarantee as the repair (*"or keep the incumbent, which the paper's ``V^m★ ≥ V^0`` holding by construction (feature 273)"*). Feature 280 (dreaming.bar) states the same reading of the guarantee for its own refusal (*"The repair is the incumbent … when nothing clears the bar, the incumbent is the argmax"*), and feature 276's ceiling and feature 271's parent rule both spell ``V^{m★} ≥ V^0`` in their prose. The member's conventions this feature follows: verdict-over-counts free functions beside the store; duck-typed seams read by getattr rather than isinstance (the module loader's synthetic-name re-execution means an isinstance would refuse the very objects composition produces); error vocabularies translated at the seam, never borrowed from a sibling's class; frozen, hand-written __slots__ values so two callers holding one cannot move each other's figure, the FreezeRecord stance CandidateModule and SweepPair take; one error base per member with subclasses split by the repair the caller must make; a code word mandated only where the feature's own sentence names one; and @register only in __init__.py, so a submodule's registration fires only on the first create_app() of a process.
- No member imports another; a member reaches a sibling through the app.* seat at call time, never through its import name. Inside the member, a shared private spelling is imported rather than respelled: cap.py imports _parsed_instant and _stamp from .cycle, and this module imports _code_hash_of from .reviser for the same reason. - Verdicts are pure functions over figures the caller already holds; the act is the store seam, and the two never share a module's job. - Error vocabularies are translated at the seam: a caller asking this feature must not meet a sibling member's class, nor feature 271's. - Values are frozen with hand-written __slots__, validated at construction, the member's FreezeRecord stance. - A restatement of another feature's rule is pinned against its owner by a test — test_cross_member.py's discipline, applied inside the member (this feature's default derived version against candidate_module's). - @register lives only in __init__.py; no new component, no seat edit, no migration, no table — feature 275's floor names that precedent.

category.name: Dreaming Loop & Meta-Selection
category.feature: System includes the incumbent policy in the candidate set, which returns a selected policy never worse on the fixed history.

project_specification.integration_points: Feature 273 is the clause that makes the 271-274 chain safe, and it is the only one of the four that three of its neighbours already cite by number while expressly disclaiming: feature 272's docstring says *"putting ``π^0 = π_t`` back into the candidate set so the selection can never fall below the current policy is feature 273's"*, feature 274's says *"It is not feature 273 either"* and draws the boundary line by line, and feature 280 (dreaming.bar) grounds its whole refusal on it — *"The repair is the incumbent, and that is what makes the refusal safe. The paper's guarantee ``V^{m★} ≥ V^0`` holds *by construction* once the incumbent is in the candidate set (feature 273's sentence): when nothing clears the bar, the incumbent *is* the argmax."* Feature 271's parent rule completes the handshake from the other direction: a candidate's ``parent_version`` is ``π_t``'s version, which is exactly the identity this feature reconstructs. ``depends_on="272"`` is the loop-ordering fact and **not** a code import — feature 272 runs the sweep whose evidence the sentence's second clause is a claim *about* (*"on the fixed history"* is the pool feature 270 holds and feature 272 crosses), and this module neither reads nor imports the sweep, the split or the store. The order the loop drives is the order the siblings' prose states: feature 275's floor refuses a thin pool, feature 276's ceiling bounds the sweep, feature 277's schedule answers ``M``, feature 271 produces the ``M`` revisions, **feature 273 includes ``π^0``**, feature 278's split marks the worlds, feature 272 sweeps the widened set and persists one row per pair, feature 274 takes the argmax under §7 and writes the winner, and feature 280 judges that winner against §12.1's bar. Where in that order the incumbent's own readings come from is deliberately *not* this feature's to fix, and both honest answers are the caller's: the widened set is what feature 272 sweeps, so the incumbent's evidence is measured on the fixed history fresh, **or** the incumbent was itself a candidate of an earlier cycle whose rows already sit in the pool under its own ``policy_version`` — and because the pool is held fixed for the iteration the two readings are the same reading. What this feature fixes is the one thing both orders need: that the candidate set feature 274's argmax ranges over contains ``π^0``. The guarantee is then a theorem about feature 274's own verdict rather than a check this module performs — the argmax is the maximum over a set containing the incumbent, so it is at least the incumbent's objective, and where it is not (a tie at the top, a candidate the objectives do not cover) feature 274 refuses rather than returning anything lower; §12.1's qualifier is honoured in this module's prose and not softened: the guarantee is about **replay score on the fixed history**, never about forward P&L. The entry this module answers is read by the producers and consumers exactly as any candidate is — feature 272 by ``module_id``, ``code_hash`` and an absent ``revision_index``; feature 274 by ``module_id`` in its argmax, by ``code_hash`` and ``parent_version`` when it writes the winner into ``policy_revision`` — and it is **duck-typed in both directions**: this module never imports :class:`~dreaming.reviser.CandidateModule` and reads a produced candidate by ``getattr``, the stance feature 272's reader states for the same reason. The module is reached directly from the member (``from dreaming import incumbent_candidate, include_incumbent, IncumbentCandidate, IncumbentRequestError``) and re-exported by the member __init__, the way feature 275's floor names and features 271-283 all are. Its one outbound coupling inside the member is :func:`~dreaming.reviser._code_hash_of`, and it is pinned: the member suite asserts this feature's default derived version equals :func:`~dreaming.reviser.candidate_module`'s default ``module_id`` for the same source, so the two derivations cannot drift into two spellings of what a candidate is — the same discipline ``test_cross_member.py`` applies across the member boundary, applied here to the one rule this feature restates.
project_specification.constraints: - Both functions are **pure**: no store, no clock, no environment, no ``@register`` component. :func:`incumbent_candidate` takes the incumbent's source and answers ``π^0`` as a candidate-shaped value; :func:`include_incumbent` takes the candidate set feature 271 produced and answers the widened set with ``π^0`` **first**. Neither opens a database, reads a row, takes a path, consults the pool or touches the loop's state — the shape :func:`dreaming.ladder.rejects_thin_pool`, feature 276's ceiling, feature 278's split, feature 279's rotation and feature 274's argmax take, and a caller that only wants the widened set asks this and pays for nothing. - :class:`IncumbentCandidate` is a **frozen value with hand-written ``__slots__``**, validated at construction, the stance :class:`~dreaming.cycle.FreezeRecord`, :class:`~dreaming.reviser.CandidateModule`, :class:`~dreaming.sweep.SweepPair` and :class:`~dreaming.cap.CapRecord` take: two callers holding one entry cannot move each other's source or identity, because the entry a caller holds is the entry the argmax ranks. Its four fields are ``source`` (the incumbent's complete policy source, non-empty text — the only thing feature 272's replay engine reads), ``code_hash`` (the sha of the source, computed by the factory, never handed in — the same rule feature 271 states for its own candidates, and the value feature 274 persists to ``policy_revision.code_hash``), ``module_id`` (the version string feature 274 writes as ``policy_revision.policy_version``) and ``parent_version`` (``None`` for an incumbent with no parent recorded in this iteration, otherwise a non-empty name). It carries **no ``revision_index``** and that absence is load-bearing, not an omission: the incumbent is not one of the ``M`` revisions feature 271 produced, feature 272's reader admits a candidate whose index is absent precisely so a sibling feature's incumbent can enter, and a fabricated index — feature 271 refuses any index below one — would mislabel the incumbent as one of the sweep's own revisions in the plan feature 272's report orders. ``__eq__`` and ``__hash__`` are the four fields, so two entries for one incumbent are one value. The class validates what it is handed and raises :class:`~dreaming.errors.IncumbentRequestError` — the ask's own vocabulary — never feature 271's :class:`~dreaming.reviser. RevisionRequestError`: the *rule* that a candidate's source and identity are non-empty text is the member's one rule, and the *vocabulary* splits by who was asked, the discipline feature 276's ceiling states for its own figures. - **One spelling of a candidate's identity.** The code hash is :func:`~dreaming.reviser._code_hash_of` imported from the member's own reviser — the private spelling feature 271's ``candidate_module`` and its deduplication share — rather than a second ``hashlib.sha256`` call here, which is the failure that function's docstring names. The **default** derived version is ``f"cand-{code_hash[:32]}"``, the same default :func:`~dreaming.reviser.candidate_module` derives for a produced revision, and it is not a coincidence worth avoiding but a property worth having: a candidate's ``module_id`` is a function of its source, so an incumbent whose caller names no ``version`` is given the very string the loop would have written for it when it *was* a candidate — a previous cycle's ``policy_revision.policy_version`` is reconstructible from the policy source alone. The restatement is pinned by a test against its owner (the same source through both derivations answers one ``module_id``) so the two cannot drift, the discipline ``test_cross_member.py`` applies across the member boundary. - :func:`include_incumbent(candidates, source, *, version=None, parent_version=None)` is the **act of including** and it answers a **tuple** with the incumbent **first** and the produced candidates in their own order after it. First, because the incumbent is the policy in force and appending it would make the loop's own report read as though a revision had been added rather than the incumbent restored; and a tuple, so the answer is a value a caller can hold and compare rather than a generator that pays again each time it is read. It **never mutates its argument**: the produced sequence is read, not consumed in place, so a caller that still needs the ``M`` revisions it produced holds them. - Both functions **refuse rather than silently defaulting**, each with :class:`~dreaming.errors.IncumbentRequestError` and naming what it is about: a source that is not non-empty text; a ``version`` that is not ``None`` or non-empty text; a ``parent_version`` that is not ``None`` or non-empty text; a candidate set that is a bare string or bytes (Python would iterate its characters and one policy source would silently become one candidate per character) or is not iterable at all; a candidate whose ``module_id`` is not non-empty text (it is how feature 274's argmax names its entrants and how the winner is written as ``policy_revision.policy_version``); a candidate whose ``code_hash`` is not non-empty text (feature 272 files one pair's evidence under it and feature 274 persists it); and — the load-bearing refusal — an incumbent that is **already in the set**, caught by its ``module_id`` or by its ``code_hash``, naming the candidate that carries it. That refusal is what makes the sentence's verb meaningful: *includes* is not *may include*, a loop that ran this feature twice has not enlarged its tournament, and a reviser that returned the incumbent's source verbatim — which feature 271's deduplication cannot catch, because it compares the revisions to *each other* and not to the incumbent they descend from — would otherwise hand feature 274 an argmax over two entrants that are one policy, or a guaranteed tie on the maximum. - An **empty** candidate set is **admitted**, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. Feature 271 refuses a production shortfall, so an empty set is a caller's own construction rather than a policy that could not fund ``M``; and the whole of this feature is *adding one*, so ``include_incumbent((), source)`` answers the one-member set ``(π^0,)`` — §C5's guarantee at its most literal, the selected policy *being* the incumbent, which is exactly what §12.1's *"when nothing clears the bar, the incumbent is the argmax"* describes from the other side. Feature 274 takes the argmax over one candidate without a tie, so the widened set is a set a selection can be taken over. This is the admission feature 276's ceiling already states for a zero revision count — *"do not run any revision is a caller's own business"* — applied one step earlier in the same loop. The refusals above still fire on an empty set: a malformed source, a malformed version or a malformed candidate set is refused whatever the set holds. - The second clause of the sentence — *"which returns a selected policy never worse on the fixed history"* — is **stated and not re-implemented**. With ``π^0`` in the set, feature 274's argmax is the maximum over a tournament one of whose entrants is the current policy, so the selected policy's §7 objective is at least the incumbent's whenever a selection is returned at all, and every path that could return something lower is feature 274's own refusal (a tie on the maximum, or a candidate the objectives do not cover). The guarantee is therefore a theorem about feature 274's verdict and this module performs **no check of it**: a function here that compared the winner's aggregate to the incumbent's would be a second spelling of the argmax's own law, and would need the objective figures feature 274 and feature 280 already rank and judge (the bar's refusal, not this one, is the case where a winner *above* the incumbent is still refused). The module's docstring states the theorem, §12.1's qualifier with it — *"a guarantee about replay score, not about future P&L"* — and the member suite pins it by running feature 274's real :func:`~dreaming.select.select_argmax` over the widened set and asserting the winner's score is at least the incumbent's, over the pool a caller actually holds. - One new error sibling under :class:`~dreaming.errors.DreamingError`, :class:`~dreaming.errors.IncumbentRequestError`, and **no code word**. Feature 275's ``pool_too_thin`` is mandated by its own sentence and this feature's sentence mandates none — its verb is *includes* — so every message opens with its subject, the stance :class:`~dreaming.errors.CapRequestError`, :class:`~dreaming.errors.RevisionCeilingError`, :class:`~dreaming.errors.HoldoutRequestError` and :class:`~dreaming.errors.TransferRequestError` state for their own pairs. The class is its own rather than a face of feature 271's :class:`~dreaming.errors.RevisionRequestError` (its repair is *re-consider the source and the version you handed the inclusion*, against *re-consider the revision sweep you asked for*), rather than feature 276's :class:`~dreaming.errors.RevisionCeilingError` (this feature refuses no count), and never feature 275's or feature 270's word: a caller that caught this refusal as any of those would act on the wrong fact. It sits beside them under the one base, so a caller that wants every failure of the dreaming path still catches one class. This feature has **no store face** — its sentence has no store act — and mints no second class. - The module is stdlib-only and import-cheap: ``typing`` and the member's own ``.reviser`` (for the one shared hash) and ``.errors``, and nothing else at module scope — no ``sqlite3``, no third-party import — so the factory's scan, which imports this package to fire its ``@register``, pays nothing for a feature it never composes. Its candidate reads are duck-typed by ``getattr``, never ``isinstance``, for the workspace's reason. **No new component** — feature 270's single ``"dreaming"`` component is the member's whole composition, and both functions are reached the way the floor, the cap, the ceiling, the split, the rotation, the bar, the comparison and the transfer are: as free functions beside the store. - The module adds four names to the member __init__ exports (:class:`IncumbentCandidate`, :class:`~dreaming.errors. IncumbentRequestError`, :func:`incumbent_candidate`, :func:`include_incumbent`), re-exported the way feature 275's floor names and features 271-283 all are, and the member's ``__all__`` is widened to carry them in its own sort order (SCREAMING_CASE, then CamelCase, then snake_case — RUF022) — the same seat-adjacency discipline the cap and the ceiling keep, so every name-sorted ``app.order`` adjacency in the existing suite is untouched (the member's one component name is unchanged, and the seat ``src/app/modules/dreaming`` still exports exactly ``{"COMPONENT_NAME", "cycle_freeze_component"}``). The sibling matrices in ``packages/dreaming/tests/test_errors.py`` widen by one method in their existing style, asserting the new class is a sibling of every class that preceded it and that neither the thin pool's nor the freeze's word is ever minted here.
